clue.text: 31 24 11 Tom was not mistaken

indicators.note: something mistaken has gone wrong, so the letters of the two words before it are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A man named Tom insists he got it right after all.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers point to 31, 24 and 11, read together as DOUBLE LEAGUE CHAMP: a manager who won the English league with two different clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Watson managed Sunderland and then Liverpool to English league titles, making him a two-club title winner.

clue.text: Difficult parting from lively woman? About right

indicators.note: About means the word for a woman goes around the letter for right

parts.note: a wench is an old word for a girl, often a lively, saucy one

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye to a spirited woman is hard, and that seems about right.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful separation or departure is called a wrench, as in leaving home being a real wrench.

clue.text: Support on course horse, English, seven years

parts.note: a tee is the peg that supports the ball on a golf course
a nag is an old or poor horse

explanation.surface: A racing tip: back an English horse aged seven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests horse racing beside 'horse', but it is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The years from thirteen to nineteen, a span of seven, make up the age group described here.

clue.text: Dislike dais — heading off

indicators.note: heading off says the word's first letter is removed

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform or dais

explanation.surface: Someone who hates platforms walks away from the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatred or strong general disapproval is meant here, a noun synonym for intense dislike.

clue.text: Law enforcer, small, went about work

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for to urinate, so went can mean peed
C, short for circa, means about
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A slight policeman went about his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went' in its lavatorial sense gives PEED, not a past tense of travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic officer who catches drivers breaking the limit is a kind of police law enforcer.

clue.text: About to get in rage over pinch

indicators.note: over tells us the combined letters are turned the other way round

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
to flip is to lose one's temper, a rage

explanation.surface: Someone is about to fly into a rage over a theft.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch is slang for to steal small things, a direct synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Eunice oddly greeting fellow with a Mexican dish

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of the name

parts.note: HI is a greeting
a lad is a fellow

explanation.surface: Eunice strangely says hello to a man holding a Mexican meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled tortilla with filling and chilli sauce is a classic dish from Mexico.

clue.text: Disturbance after drink in vehicle

indicators.note: after puts the disturbance word behind the drink word

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea, a drink
a riot is a public disturbance

explanation.surface: A drunken disturbance breaks out in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage of ancient warfare is an early example of a vehicle.

clue.text: Postscript about Reformed pastor's musical favourites

indicators.note: about means the postscript letters go around the rest
Reformed means the word pastor is put into a new shape

explanation.surface: A note added about a church minister's favourite hymns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' suggests the Protestant church, but it signals a rearrangement of PASTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrated pop performers are favourites in the music business, hence musical favourites.

clue.text: Plaintive legal ace I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so the letters before it are arranged freshly

explanation.surface: A mournful lawyer muses about being a top courtroom performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mournful, lamenting writing or tone is both elegiac and plaintive, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Reportedly win horse chestnut

indicators.note: Reportedly says the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: to conquer is to win

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a horse called Chestnut won.
explanation.walkthrough: Conkers is a British children's game played with horse chestnuts on strings.
explanation.definitionFit: The shiny brown seed of the horse chestnut tree is the familiar name used by British children.

clue.text: Best bite

definitions.meaning: short for champion, the best of all

explanation.surface: Choosing the finest mouthful.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is slang for a winner, the best; as a verb it means to munch or chew.

clue.text: 31 24 11 Herbert's rewritten 11 article

indicators.note: rewritten shows the letters of the 11 answer are arranged afresh

parts.note: the answer to 11 across, meaning best
AN is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Herbert has redrafted an article about a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Chapman led Huddersfield Town and then Arsenal to English league titles, so he won with two clubs.

clue.text: Coming back, do bathroom up maybe first for superior type

indicators.note: Coming back says the decorating word is read backwards

parts.note: to tile is one way to renovate a bathroom
1ST, written IST, is short for first

explanation.surface: A snob insists on redecorating the bathroom first on returning home.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who thinks they belong to a select, better group is a superior or snobbish type.

clue.text: Club overcoming Everton's outside threat

indicators.note: overcoming means the club goes over, around, the other letters

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club

indicators.note: outside picks the outer letters of the football club's name

explanation.surface: A football club sees off a threat from Everton's wingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a football team beside Everton, but it is a weapon. Everton is a Liverpool football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A danger or source of harm is a menace, a straightforward synonym for threat.

clue.text: Good to get involved in new alliance? Very good!

indicators.note: to get involved in says the good letter is placed inside the rearranged letters
new means the word alliance is made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A decent man joins a fresh coalition, and it is excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Like an angel is the meaning, and an angel is the model of being exceedingly good.

clue.text: Partly missing urban term for joking

indicators.note: Partly missing says the answer is the words with parts left off at each end, the letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A city slang word for joking has fallen out of use.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful teasing talk is banter, a noun naming the activity of joking.

clue.text: Certificate Heath maybe's written in advance

parts.note: scrip is a certificate of share ownership
Ted Heath was a British Prime Minister, so Ted is an example name for him

explanation.surface: Edward Heath's certificate was drafted ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath was the UK Conservative Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: Prepared or set down on paper beforehand, as a scripted speech is, is the meaning.

clue.text: Like flier following ship?

parts.note: as means like
a tern is a seabird, a flier

explanation.surface: Like a bird trailing a vessel at sea?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface picture of a seabird following a ship is the definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: At or towards the rear of a vessel, behind it, is the nautical meaning of being behind a ship.

clue.text: 31 24 11 Brian at first cited Neagh maybe

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of the word cited

parts.note: Lough Neagh in Northern Ireland is an example of a lough, an Irish lake

explanation.surface: Brian was first mentioned near a famous Irish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Clough won the English league with Derby County and then Nottingham Forest, two different clubs.

clue.text: Referring to some numbers Adrian regularly used in exam

indicators.note: used in puts the picked letters inside the exam word

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam

indicators.note: regularly picks every second letter of the name

explanation.surface: Adrian often used figures in his test.
explanation.definitionFit: First, second and third are numbers showing order, and the adjective for such numbers is this.

clue.text: Blemish by church rarely seen

parts.note: a scar is a blemish
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A mark beside the church is seldom noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in short supply and hard to find is scarce, so it is seldom seen.

clue.text: Starts off creating original unit leaving other measures behind — this one?

indicators.note: Starts off picks the first letter of each following word

parts.words: creating original unit leaving other measures behind

explanation.surface: A new unit of measure is invented and leaves the others behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The words both build the answer and describe it, as the unit is named after its originator.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of electric charge is an original unit of measure, the one the clue points at.

clue.text: After hearing, understand America's head count

indicators.note: After hearing says the words are taken as spoken

parts.note: to sense something is to understand it; US stands for the United States, America

explanation.surface: Once the evidence is heard, the US gets the number of people.
explanation.definitionFit: An official count of a population, literally counting heads, is the meaning.

clue.text: Competition distance once used

definitions.meaning: a sporting contest between teams over a season
an old measure of distance, about three miles

explanation.surface: A race over an old-fashioned length.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a contest between many teams and an obsolete unit of about three miles.

clue.text: Home mostly lacking interest, say — brought over drink?

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: dull means lacking interest

indicators.note: brought over says the letters for say are turned backwards

parts.note: EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: Bored at home, someone has a drink brought over.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as loose: to indulge can mean to drink alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: To indulge is to allow oneself a treat, and in context to enjoy alcohol freely.

clue.text: Omit old crossword feature to accommodate daughter

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: to accommodate means the clue word takes the daughter letter inside

parts.note: a clue is part of every crossword

explanation.surface: Leave out an old crossword clue to make room for a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave out or not include something is the plain synonym for omit.

clue.text: Some reach a country plain

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some travellers reach a country of flat land.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gran Chaco is a vast lowland region of South America, an example of a plain.

clue.text: Key mixer

definitions.meaning: in music, the first note of a scale, the keynote
a drink added to spirits, as with gin

explanation.surface: An essential social mingler.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the keynote of a musical key and also the water often mixed with gin.

clue.text: In which player's accompanied wrong female — almost gone off

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
gal is a casual word for a female

indicators.note: off, meaning gone bad, signals the remaining letters are jumbled
almost says the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A musician played along with the wrong woman before nearly vanishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A session where a pianist or guitarist plays while everyone joins in the song fits the definition.

clue.text: 31 24 11 Kenny glad to go back at 51. Scottish? Extremely

indicators.note: to go back says the word glad is read in reverse

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: Extremely picks the two end letters of the word Scottish

explanation.surface: Kenny is pleased to return at 51, and very Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenny Dalglish managed Liverpool and Blackburn Rovers to English league titles, winning with two clubs.

clue.text: At party strange blue drink, large

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: strange tells us the letters of blue are rearranged

explanation.surface: At a party someone orders a weird blue cocktail, a big one.
explanation.definitionFit: A twice-sized measure of spirits is the bar name for a large drink.
